label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8), first-token dependent
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at the delimiter step (86% of activation mass; 11% of delimiter steps), with a small tail on the first one or two copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, ~13% of mass). It essentially never fires during the original phase. It is strongly gated by length: rate rises steeply with L (none for L<=4, rare for L 5-7, most mass at L=8 and 9; t=9 holds 62% of mass). Within long-sequence delimiter steps, whether and how strongly it fires depends on the first original token (the token about to be output): first token m or v gives ~72% precision and the top activations, while r, l, n, y, g, x, f rarely fire (<16%). The dependence is graded rather than a clean set, so a first-token set adds only ~5 F1 points and is left out. Precision of the simple predicate is low (~0.30) because many L>=8 delimiter steps stay inactive.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: v, m, t, u; copy phase: m, k, 3, v; input phase: ) and the third original token (most: h, x, e, n, r, z; least: b, p, q, a); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=8.
